explanations: The return value of out.write() is ignored. When the destination disk or file stream is slower than gunzip + parsing, write() returns false but the loop keeps reading and writing, so the writable's internal buffer grows without bound. A multi-gigabyte batch can be held almost entirely in memory and crash the worker. The loop should await once(out, 'drain') whenever write() returns false so backpressure propagates back to the read side.

The loop checks Buffer.byteLength(line) > opts.maxLineBytes, increments stats.rejected and continues. Nothing throws, nothing truncates, and the oversize line never reaches out.write. Note that readline still had to assemble the full line in memory before the check runs.
The 'data' listener is attached to raw, the file read stream, before gunzip, so it counts compressed bytes. Decompressed and output sizes are never measured, and rejected lines are not excluded.
readline's async iterator rejects when its input stream errors, so the for-await throws; finally closes lines and destroys raw, then the error propagates. There is no retry and no swallowing.
